question.text: This empire located in the Indian subcontinent was founded by Babur. Shah Jahan who built the Taj Mahal, was a ruler of this empire.
question.clue: This empire was founded after the defeat of Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat.

swap.text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah is considered the father of this nation, which split from India in 1947. This nation still disputes the Kashmir province with India.
swap.clue: Following its independence, this country's southern border was demarcated by the Radcliffe Line.

question.text: After he murdered Mahatma Gandhi, Godse was put on trial in the Red Fort of this Indian city. A "New" district of this city is the capital of India.
question.clue: Plans for George VI to impress the "native minds" of this city by traveling to it via plane to hold a grand ceremony at Coronation Park were dropped because of their lack of political or financial tact.

swap.leadin: This man achieved his goals using satyagraha, or the force of truth.
swap.text: Name this leader who advocated nonviolence to help India achieve independence. In 1948, he was assassinated by Nathuram Godse.
swap.clue: This this man led a March to Dandi which led to a declaration of Pura Swaraj, or complete self-rule.

question.leadin: A monument for an incident at this location was erected by Lord Curzon in front of St. John's Church in 1901.
question.text: Name this prison during the Third Carnatic War in which 123 British prisoners of war died in one night from suffocation and heat exhaustion because of the cramped conditions.
question.clue: This event's 123 victims primarily died of heat exhaustion in Fort William, where they had been captured by the Nawab of Bengal.

swap.leadin: Identify these historical people, who all hold the honorary title of 'father of the nation'.
swap.text: This man assumed leadership of his country's National Congress in 1921. His 'salt march'in 1930 emphasised his commitment to non-violent protest against the British Empire.
swap.answerHtml: Mahatma Gandhi [prompt on just Gandhi by asking ‘which one?’]
swap.clue: He encouraged his countrymen to join him on a protest known as the Salt March.
swap.set: 2023 Politics & History with a side of Memes

question.text: The Bofors scandal led to the downfall of an Indian politician with this surname. Other people with this surname included Indira and the leader of the Indian independence movement, Mahatma.
question.answerHtml: Gandhi (accept Rajiv Gandhi or Indira Gandhi or Mahatma Gandhi)
question.clue: A politician with this surname instituted forced sterilization and removed civil liberties during a period dubbed "The Emergency."

swap.leadin: This leader's government attempted to implicate labor leader George Fernandes in the Baroda Dynamite Case, but Fernandes successfully ran for Parliament from prison.
swap.text: Name this leader who wielded near-absolute power during a 21-month-long period known as the Emergency. This leader later ordered the controversial Operation Blue Star.
swap.clue: This leader ordered air strikes in response to Operation Chingiz Khan to support a "Liberation War" against a 1971 genocide launched by Operation Searchlight.

question.leadin: A 1963 crisis in this region developed after a strand of the Prophet Mohammad's hair was stolen from a shrine in Hazratbal.
question.text: Identify this region claimed by both India and Pakistan on opposite sides of the Line of Control. It should not be confused with Punjab.
question.clue: The Glancy Commission investigated a 1931 massacre committed in this region by troops of its repressive Dogra dynasty.

swap.leadin: Arab spice traders established the Ketchchimalai ("catch-chi-mah-lie") Mosque in this island's settlement of Beruwala, where they first landed.
swap.text: Name this island, which was given the name "Serendib" by Arab traders. Adam's Bridge connects this island to the mainland.
swap.clue: Failing irrigation tanks triggered the Great Famine in this country's Anuradhapura Kingdom, which fell to Chola invasions.

question.leadin: Identify these events from the British colonization of India.
question.text: Cartridges of Enfield Rifles greased with pork fat incited this uprising in 1857, which began in Meerut after the Bahadur Shah was proclaimed emperor and was put down by Colin Campbell.
question.clue: This event saw the death of Henry Lawrence in the Siege of Lucknow.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Indian history.
swap.text: The southernmost kingdoms in India and Sri Lanka remained independent of the Mauryan Empire. They were primarily of this ethnicity. Their namesake "tigers" were a terrorist group in Sri Lanka until 2009.
swap.clue: This ethnic group created "singing steps" leading up to one of their three "Great Living" temples; that temple depicted legends associated with 63 "poet-saints" of this ethnicity.

question.leadin: A prime minister from this family was deposed by a military council during Operation Fair Play.
question.text: Since its 1967 founding, leadership of the PPP party has been held by the Zadaris and what other family? In 1988, a member of this family became the first woman to be elected head of government of a Muslim-majority country.
question.clue: One member of this family was ousted and executed by Zia-ul-Haq's July 5th coup while another member of this family was assassinated by a suicide bomb at Liaqat National Park in December, 2007.

swap.text: The day after the mosque's invasion, protesters burned down this city's U.S. embassy. It replaced Karachi as Pakistan's capital in 1961.
swap.clue: Built in 1960, name this city that became the capital of a South Asian nation that split from India in 1947.

question.text: In 1993, this third President of Sri Lanka was killed by the Tamil Tigers. He had previously given arms to them to help them rid Sri Lanka of the Indian Peace Keeping Force, but this proved counter-productive.

swap.leadin: One of these objects named for the Allahabad Fort includes Late Brahmi inscriptions added by the Gupta, who built an "iron" one in Delhi.
swap.text: Name this type of object which an earlier ruler topped with a statue of four lions and an abacus at Sarnath.
swap.answerHtml: pillars [or columns; or pillar edicts; prompt on poles; prompt on edicts by asking “recorded on what objects?”]
swap.clue: One of these objects made of sandstone at Sarnath ("SAR-not") was originally topped with an abacus and lion capital.

question.text: The Amritsar protestors were expressing opposition to these laws, which addressed Indian sedition by removing the rights of warrant, habeas corpus, and appeal from those subject to the British Raj.
question.clue: Also known as the "Black Acts," name this 1919 legislation which was passed over the unanimous opposition of the Indian members of the Supreme Legislative Council.

swap.text: Aw Barkhadle may have also spread Islam to this present-day country. Arabic partially inspired the right-to-left Thaana ("TAH-nuh") script for this country's Dhivehi ("dih-VAY-hee") language.
swap.answerHtml: Maldives [or Republic of Maldives; accept Maldive Islands or Sultanate of Maldives]
swap.clue: In the 20th century, this country was long led by the dictator Maumoon Abdul Gayoom, who sparked civil unrest in 2005 by arresting the main opposition figure, Mohamed Nasheed.

question.text: This successor of Rajaraja I conquered the Srivijaya kingdom, the Pegu islands, and managed to extract credit from Khmer.

swap.leadin: One apocryphal account in this religion's history holds that the sixty-nine-year-old Baba Deep held his severed head on his body while storming a holy city in 1757.
swap.text: Name this religion whose members were massacred in the Chhota and Wadda Holocausts, which occurred in 1746 and 1762 at the hands of Lakhpat Rai and Ahmad Shah Abdali.
swap.clue: That monarch who followed this religion defeated the Afghan king Zaman Shah to capture Lahore, then declared himself a maharaja.
